The Mother of God: Sweet Kissing

Glykophilousa · Sweet Kiss

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Sweet Kissing names a tender Mother-and-Child composition. The OCA describes the particular venerated Glykophilousa at Philotheou Monastery on Mount Athos. The artwork shown here is a historical example of the type, not a claim to be the Philotheou original.

[1] Final two paragraphs

What is depicted

The Mother of God inclines toward Christ as he embraces her. The OCA places this composition within the Eleousa, or Virgin of Tenderness, category and remarks on the unusually close embrace and affectionate expression of the Philotheou image.

[1] Penultimate paragraph

History and tradition

According to the tradition recounted by the OCA, Victoria preserved an icon from her iconoclast husband during the reign of Theophilos by casting it into the sea. It arrived at Athos, where the monks of Philotheou received it. The account associates a spring with the landing place and records a Bright Monday procession. It locates the venerated image on a pillar at the left of the monastery’s main church and gives March 27 and Bright Monday as its commemorations.

[1] Opening two paragraphs; final two paragraphs

Published explanation

The source presents the affection exchanged by Christ and his Mother as the characteristic of this type. The rescue-at-sea account belongs to Philotheou’s sacred tradition; another historical Glykophilousa image need not share that object’s individual provenance.

[1] Opening and penultimate paragraphs
